title: EIP-8425: Quantum Freeze and Account Recovery
description: Freezes protocol-validated secp256k1 signatures and recovers unmigrated accounts by seed proof.
author: Liyi Guo (@colinlyguo)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract Before the freeze, owners can migrate to quantum-resistant wallet code at the same address through [EIP-8298](./eip-8298.md). The freeze rejects transactions carrying protocol-validated secp256k1 signatures and removes the `ecRecover` precompile. An owner who missed migration can install successor code at the same address with a hash-based zero-knowledge proof of the wallet seed. ## Motivation A practical quantum break of secp256k1 could expose unmigrated accounts. Specifying a response in advance lets clients and wallets implement, test and audit it before an emergency, reducing coordination under time pressure. Whether to activate this response, when to do so, or whether to choose another course remains a separate decision. ## Specification ### Parameters | Parameter | Value | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `QUANTUM_FREEZE_TIME` | TBD | Activation timestamp (Unix seconds) | | `RECOVER` | `0x07` | Recovery frame mode | | `SEED_PROOF_GAS` | 2000000 | Execution gas per proof verification attempt | The network may schedule the timestamp in advance or coordinate an earlier one in an emergency. Nodes must agree on it before activation. ### Freeze For blocks with `block.timestamp >= QUANTUM_FREEZE_TIME`, reject before execution any transaction containing a protocol-validated secp256k1 ECDSA signature. This applies to transactions with a secp256k1 sender signature (including [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) transactions) and to [EIP-8141](./eip-8141.md) transactions whose `signatures` list contains a `SECP256K1` entry. Existing delegations remain callable. Remove the `ecRecover` precompile at `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001` and its automatic [EIP-2929](./eip-2929.md) prewarming. Preserve the account state. Ordinary account and gas rules apply to all call types. Successful calls to the empty code return empty data. A successful `CALL` transfers forwarded value, and a revert rolls back that transfer. ### Mnemonic recovery The wallet locally derives the 64-byte [BIP-39](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/0d99ffd39fdaf75209c43b1f8ec3fbbc23f10814/bip-0039.mediawiki) seed using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 (2048 iterations). Use the mnemonic as the password and `"mnemonic" + passphrase` as the salt, normalizing each string to NFKD before encoding it in UTF-8. The default passphrase is empty. A backup of the seed bytes grants the same authority. #### Submission and execution From the freeze timestamp, an EIP-8141 transaction may include `RECOVER` only as its last frame, outside any atomic batch, with an explicit 20-byte target, zero flags and zero value. Its data is exactly 222,760 bytes, comprising a 92-byte header with a big-endian uint64 nonce followed by the proof. ```text be8(nonce) || source || code_hash || tag || proof ``` Violating these constraints invalidates the transaction. A sponsor may approve payment in an earlier frame and pays ordinary frame-data charges. The target needs neither a signature nor ETH. Charge and warm the target at frame entry under EIP-8141. Record each charged target or source access in the block-level access list even if the frame later reverts. Dispatch directly even for a delegated target. Use live account state after any earlier frame or batch rollback. Use EIP-8298's definition of a system contract and its `SETCODEFROM` rules for source eligibility, adoption costs and code-hash recording. 1. Require prior payment approval and the target's current nonce to equal `nonce`. Its own code must be empty or exactly `0xef0100` followed by a 20-byte address. An absent target has nonce zero and empty code. Reject precompiles, system contracts and targets created by contract creation in this transaction. 2. Charge for source access and validation, then warm the source. Require an eligible source whose current `codeHash` equals `code_hash`. 3. Charge `SEED_PROOF_GAS` before decoding the proof or reconstructing the journal. Verify the [proof](#proof-system) against the [expected journal](#proof-statement). 4. Charge the remaining current-account and write costs. Charge EIP-8141 account-creation state gas if the target has zero nonce, zero balance and empty code. Install the authorized code hash and record the change. Preserve target nonce, balance and storage. Return success with empty logs, without executing wallet code. A failed execution check reverts the frame. Insufficient gas causes an exceptional halt. EIP-8141 frame charging and rollback apply, including rollback of address warmth. #### Proof statement Use [BIP-32](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/0d99ffd39fdaf75209c43b1f8ec3fbbc23f10814/bip-0032.mediawiki) private derivation along `m/44'/60'/a'/c/i`, with unsigned `a, i < 2**31` and `c` equal to 0 or 1. Use compressed SEC1 public keys for non-hardened steps. Reject an invalid master key or child at the specified index. For the resulting secp256k1 point `(x, y)`, derive `account = keccak256(be32(x) || be32(y))[12:]`. `beN` encodes an unsigned integer in exactly `N` big-endian bytes. Addresses are 20 bytes, hashes are 32 bytes, and the domain string is ASCII. The guest reads the 168-byte witness with `a` encoded before hardening. ```text witness = seed || be4(a) || be4(c) || be4(i) || be32(chain_id) || be8(nonce) || source || code_hash intent = "EIP-8425/recover/v1" || be32(chain_id) || account || be8(nonce) || source || code_hash tag = HMAC-SHA-256(key=seed, message=intent) public_input_hash = keccak256(intent || tag) journal = account || tag || public_input_hash ``` Only the 84-byte journal is public output. The verifier reconstructs it using the current chain ID, the frame target as `account`, and the header fields, including the supplied `tag`. #### Proof system The frame carries a native RISC Zero zkVM 3.1.0 succinct STARK for the [recovery guest](../assets/eip-8425/zk/guest/src/main.rs).
